data.name: Nidah
data.gender_notes: Nidah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic verb ‘nadaha’, meaning ‘to flow’. This name refers to the monthly menstrual cycle that women undergo, which is a natural process and a sign of fertility. The name Nidah carries the meaning “Menstruation” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Nidah usually hope their child will grow to embody menstruation and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder of Allah's divine plan and the miracle of creation.
data.etymology: Nidah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Menstruation.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nidah total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

The name Nidah is associated with a person who is devoid of imagination and creativity, and is often used to describe a person who is melancholic or sorrowful.

data.cultural_impact: In Islamic culture, the name "Nidah" refers to the holy period when a menstruating woman is considered impure and must stay away from the Masjid (mosque) and other religious gatherings. She can only resume prayers and attend religious activities once her menstrual cycle is over and she has taken a Ghusl ( ritual bath). This practice is based on Hadith and Quranic verses that emphasize the importance of cleanliness and keeping oneself pure before Allah (God).
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Nidah" holds spiritual significance as it is a reminder of the natural cycles of life and the importance of self-reflection and purification. The menstrual cycle is a reminder of the power and capacity of womanhood, and it is a time for self-care, rest, and renewal. It is also a time to remember and honor the sanctity of the body, which is a vessel for the soul and a gift from Allah.
